speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your scalp and forehead, and how long it has been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Does your baby seem itchy or uncomfortable, and is there any crusting or oozing from the rash?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: The greasy yellow scales and erythematous patches are very characteristic. Are there any similar patches in the diaper area or behind the ears?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Premature birth (36 weeks), otherwise generally healthy. Family history of psoriasis. Social history: The patient is 3 months old, so the social history is not applicable.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the greasy yellow scales, erythematous patches, and the distribution on the scalp and forehead of a 3-month-old infant, this presentation is classic for infantile seborrheic dermatitis, also known as cradle cap. The worsening in cold weather and family history of psoriasis are noted, but the greasy nature of the scales strongly favors seborrhea over psoriasis in this age group. I have sufficient information to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis
